title: 8 משחקים וספרים שיעזרו להם להתרכז ולחכות

stage.need: Attention and self-regulation (waiting, stopping, following a rule) around ages 4 to 5. CDC 5 years: 'Pays attention for 5 to 10 minutes during activities' and 'Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children'; CDC 4 years: teach a child to stop and wait through games like red light, green light; Harvard GSE: simple games with rules support executive function and self-regulation at ages 4 to 7. Games give the waiting a reason, books give a story about patience.
stage.age_caveat: Ages are approximate: CDC milestones are what most children (75% or more) do by an age, not a deadline. Some 4 year olds hold their attention for a long game and some 5 year olds need more time; the frame says בסביבות and the caption says יש ילדים ש....

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early. (date reviewed 16 May 2026)
dev_sources.quote: Pays attention for 5 to 10 minutes during activities. / Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children. / Teach your child to follow rules in games. / Play games that help with memory and attention. / Read books and talk about the feelings characters have and why they have them. / Talk about and label your child's and your own feelings.
dev_sources.supports: 5 year milestones and tips: attention for 5 to 10 minutes in activities, following rules and taking turns in games, playing games for memory and attention, and reading books while talking about characters' feelings. The CDC site blocks plain curl, so the page was read through a page fetch and the sentences are quoted as returned, joined with ' / '.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 4 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early. (date reviewed 16 May 2026)
dev_sources.quote: Teach your child to stop and wait when excited by playing red light, green light, or freeze dance / Continue to teach your child skills to play with others, such as using words, sharing toys, and taking turns. / Comforts others who are hurt or sad, like hugging a crying friend / Help your child learn about others' feelings, and about positive ways to react. / Comfort your child if he is afraid and talk about his fears.
dev_sources.supports: 4 year tips and milestones: practise stopping and waiting through games, taking turns, comforting someone who is sad, learning about others' feelings and talking about fears. Read through a page fetch (the CDC site blocks plain curl); quoted as returned, joined with ' / '.

dev_sources.title: Play Helps Children Build Better Brains. Here Are Some Ways to Get Kids Learning
dev_sources.publisher: Harvard Graduate School of Education, Usable Knowledge (Ryan Nagelhout, 14 Jan 2025)
dev_sources.quote: Children's activities like "freeze dance," "Simon says," and "I spy" are classics for a reason.
dev_sources.supports: For ages 4 to 7 the article lists simple games with rules as classics for building executive function and self-regulation (the page fetch summarised the last phrase; only the quoted sentence is verbatim). A reputable explainer of the Center on the Developing Child's guidance, not primary research.
